chapters.name: Accounting Principles and Journal Entries
chapters.introduction: Accounting is the systematic recording of financial transactions. Covers basic principles, types of accounts, and journal entry rules.
chapters.whyItMatters: 20-25 marks. Journal entries form the foundation of every accounting exam.

topics.name: Golden Rules of Accounting
topics.explanation: Three types of accounts: (1) Personal Account — Debit the receiver, credit the giver. (2) Real Account — Debit what comes in, credit what goes out. (3) Nominal Account — Debit all expenses/losses, credit all incomes/gains.
keyPoints: Real: Dr what comes in, Cr what goes out
topics.examTip: Identify the account type first before applying the rule.

topics.name: Journal Entry Format
topics.explanation: A journal entry records a transaction with Date | Particulars | L.F. | Debit Amount | Credit Amount. Every entry must balance (Debit = Credit). Narration is written below in brackets explaining the transaction.
topics.examTip: Never forget the narration — it carries marks.

chapters.name: Posting to Ledger
chapters.introduction: The ledger is the principal book of accounts. Journalized transactions are posted to individual T-accounts (ledger accounts). Balancing closes each account to find the net balance.
chapters.whyItMatters: 15-20 marks. Ledger posting and balancing questions are standard.

topics.name: Balancing Ledger Accounts
topics.explanation: After posting all entries to a T-account, total both sides. If Debit > Credit: balance c/d on credit side (Debit Balance). If Credit > Debit: balance c/d on debit side (Credit Balance). Bring forward the balance as b/d on the opposite side for the next period.
topics.examTip: Draw the T-account clearly, post all entries, then balance.

topics.name: Trial Balance and Error Correction
topics.explanation: Trial balance lists all ledger account balances. Total Dr = Total Cr proves arithmetical accuracy. Does NOT detect: errors of omission, commission, compensation, and principle. Common corrections: suspense account for one-sided errors.
keyPoints: Trial Balance is NOT a final account
Errors it cannot detect: complete omission, wrong account posting
topics.examTip: Show the DR and CR columns with totals matching. Marks are given for correct column totals.

chapters.name: Trading Account, P&L Account, and Balance Sheet
chapters.introduction: Final accounts summarise the financial performance and position of a business. Trading Account shows gross profit. Profit & Loss Account shows net profit. Balance Sheet shows financial position.
chapters.whyItMatters: 25-30 marks. The highest-weighted section. Questions always appear.

topics.name: Trading and Profit & Loss Account
topics.explanation: Trading Account: Dr side — Opening Stock + Purchases + Direct Expenses. Cr side — Sales + Closing Stock. Gross Profit = Cr side − Dr side. P&L Account: Dr — Gross Loss + Indirect Expenses. Cr — Gross Profit + Non-operating Income. Net Profit = Cr − Dr.
keyPoints: Direct expenses go to Trading Account
Indirect expenses go to P&L Account
topics.examTip: Memorise which expenses are direct vs indirect. This differentiates average from top scores.
topics.formula:
Gross Profit = (Sales + Closing Stock) − (Opening Stock + Purchases + Direct Exp)
Net Profit = Gross Profit + Other Income − Indirect Expenses

topics.name: Balance Sheet
topics.explanation: Balance Sheet shows assets and liabilities at a point in time. Left side (Liabilities): Capital + Net Profit − Drawings, Long-term liabilities, Current liabilities. Right side (Assets): Fixed assets, Current assets (Cash, Debtors, Stock).
keyPoints: Current ratio = Current Assets / Current Liabilities
topics.examTip: If balance sheet doesn't balance, check net profit/loss is correctly transferred.
topics.formula:
Assets = Capital + Liabilities
Working Capital = Current Assets − Current Liabilities
